data.long_meaning: Goddess of the waters and fertility, who is believed to protect the newborn and children. The name Anahid carries the meaning “Moon Goddess” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Persian. Parents who choose Anahid usually hope their child will grow to embody moon goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Anahid belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon Goddess.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anahid total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Anahid is of Armenian origin, and she is considered the goddess of water, fertility, and love in Armenian mythology. In ancient Armenia, the Anahid temple was one of the most significant religious sites, and many pilgrims visited it to ensure the protection and welfare of their children.
data.spiritual_significance: Anahid represents the nurturing aspects of nature, providing sustenance to all life through water and fertility. Symbolically, her name signifies the importance of water as a source of life and spiritual renewal. Furthermore, Anahid is a protector of newborns, emphasizing the idea that new life and spiritual growth begin with the aquatic journey in the womb.

historical_references.reference: Anahid was believed to be a goddess of fertility and love in the ancient Persian culture, particularly in Armenia.
historical_references.context: Anahid is mentioned in various ancient texts, including inscriptions and works of literature, as a deity revered by the ancient Persians and Armenians.

historical_references.reference: The name 'Anahid' was later adopted by a Sufi saint and poet, Sheikh Anahita, during the 13th century in the Islamic world. Sheikh Anahita was known for his spiritual teachings and poetry, and his name served to preserve the memory of the ancient goddess in the Islamic tradition.
historical_references.context: Sheikh Anahita's followers saw him as a manifestation of the ancient goddess Anahid, and her attributes of love and fertility were associated with his spiritual teachings.

modern_usage.modern_context: Anahid, an Islamic name of Persian origin meaning 'the immortal', has gained popularity in modern contexts due to various trends.
